findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσωνται παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου λήψονται.
findings.english_quote: The1891 editor conjectured ask in III.9 against reported Athos will hear.
findings.issue: Footnote h misattributes the asking conjecture. The supplied LH1891 report identifies it as Anger’s conjecture, whereas the note credits the 1891 editor with originating it. This is a provenance defect, not a reason to replace the selected asking reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the sentence to: “The 1891 working edition adopts Anger’s conjecture ‘ask’ in III.9 against the reported Athos reading ‘will hear.’” Retain the distinction between partly preserved papyrus letters and the supplied final iota. The proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσωνται παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου λήψονται.
findings.english_quote: The1891 editor conjectured ask in III.9 against reported Athos will hear.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently reproduces the same unsupported attribution in footnote h. The supplied report attributes the conjecture to Anger, not to the 1891 editor. Its main-text asking promise remains compatible with the selected working source.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the sentence to: “The 1891 working edition adopts Anger’s conjecture ‘ask’ in III.9 against the reported Athos reading ‘will hear.’” Preserve the existing disclosure of partial papyrus preservation and editorial supplementation. Review the replacement before acceptance.

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the selected Greek, with the simplified edition assessed independently. Their main texts preserve the passage’s requirements, negations, comparative glory, asking promise, and dialogue without a concrete fidelity defect identified. Both need a minor correction to the attribution in footnote h. This review assesses compatibility with the supplied working source and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
